title: Six pull requests merged in three minutes over a failing ci-ok, and main went red for over an hour

first_order.what_broke: PR #460 added `scripts/pr_triage.py` with no row in the ops-console tool registry. Its own CI failed on `tests/unit/test_console_tools_run.py::test_console_tool_registry_has_no_drift` at 21:46:09Z and named the file. `ci-ok` failed with it. The PR merged 19 minutes later anyway and main went red. It was not alone: six PRs merged between 22:05:14Z and 22:08:25Z — #458, #460, #457, #456, #455, #463 — every one with `merged_by: chidionyema` and `auto_merge: null`.
first_order.receipt: gh pr view 460 --json statusCheckRollup at merge time: `changes=FAILURE guard=CANCELLED python=SKIPPED ci-ok=FAILURE`, merged_at 2026-08-19T22:05:30Z. Failing job log 96234883271: `AssertionError: ... assert not ['scripts/pr_triage.py']` at 21:46:09Z. Attribution: `gh api repos/chidionyema/prospector/pulls/{455,456,457,458,460,463} -q .merged_by.login` returns `chidionyema` for all six; automerge.yml merges with secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN and is always attributed to app/github-actions, so none of these were automerge.
first_order.fixed_by: PR #474 registered the tool (peer session); PR #472 restores the innocent commit the green guard removed.

cause_chain: A tool landed on main without the ops-console row its own test requires.
The test caught it on the PR, 19 minutes before the merge. The evidence existed and was ignored.

Nothing refused the merge. Native branch protection is unavailable on this GitHub plan — `403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro` on both /branches/main/protection and /rulesets — so `ci-ok` is a required check in name only.

`~/.claude/scripts/rule-guard.py::_merge_refusal` fences a `gh pr merge` typed into a shell on this box. It cannot see a merge made from the GitHub web UI, and six merges in three minutes and fourteen seconds is the shape of a web UI session, not of six shell commands.

CLASS: a rule enforced only at one of several entry points is not enforced. The guard covers the entry an agent uses and leaves the entry a person uses wide open, so the estate believes it is protected while the most common path is unguarded.

second_order.note: RUN 2026-08-19. The six are the incident itself; the sweep is what establishes that they are a batch rather than one slip, which is what moves the diagnosis from 'someone made a mistake' to 'the path is unguarded'. Not fixed, because the fix is not a code change to those PRs — it is a refusal that reaches the web UI, and the only mechanism that can is a required status check, which needs a paid plan. That is a founder decision and is named as one below.

third_order.mechanism: NOT LANDED. Three candidates, cheapest first: (1) `.github/workflows/main-green-guard.yml` already reverts a red main, so the damage is bounded — but it reverts the HEAD, not the cause, which is its own incident. (2) A `workflow_run` job that comments on and re-opens any PR merged while its own `ci-ok` was not SUCCESS: detection, not refusal, but it reaches every entry point. (3) GitHub Pro, which makes `ci-ok` a genuinely required check and refuses the merge in the UI itself. Only (3) is a real refusal, and it costs money, so it is the founder's call.
third_order.note: Documented in docs/CI_DEBUG_RUNBOOK.md under 'What is guarded, and what is still only words' — listed as an admission, not a plan.

grade.signature: a pull request whose merge commit lands while its own ci-ok check is not SUCCESS
